title: Basic Mensuration
tagline: Year 2 — Perimeter, area and volume of common shapes

introduction.overview: Mensuration is the measurement of shapes: perimeter (length around), area (surface covered) and volume (space occupied). A small set of formulas covers rectangles, squares, triangles, circles, trapeziums, cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres. The skill is in choosing the right formula and keeping units consistent (cm, cm², cm³).
introduction.placementRelevance: Mensuration questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds, often combined with ratio, percentage and cost.
introduction.realWorldContext: Painting a wall, tiling a floor, filling a tank and fencing a field all use these formulas.

learningObjectives: Compute perimeter and area of plane figures
Compute volume and surface area of common solids
Handle paths and borders around rectangles
Use percentage changes in dimensions to find the change in area

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Use π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7, and 3.14 otherwise, unless π is left in the answer.

coreDefinitions: Perimeter: total length of the boundary. Area: surface enclosed. Volume: space enclosed by a solid.
Total surface area (TSA): area of all faces; lateral (curved) surface area (CSA): area of the sides only.
Units: length cm, area cm², volume cm³; 1 m³ = 1000 litres.
Radius r, diameter d = 2r, height h, slant height l.
Trapezium: a quadrilateral with one pair of parallel sides.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Area counts squares and volume counts cubes. Doubling every length multiplies area by 4 and volume by 8. This scaling idea explains the percentage-change problems.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write the formula, substitute with units, and check the answer has the right units. Use 22/7 for circles with radius 7, 14, 21.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Rectangle and square
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Area = l × b;  Perimeter = 2(l + b);  Square: a², 4a

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Triangle and trapezium
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Triangle = ½ × base × height;  Trapezium = ½ (a + b) h

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cuboid and cube
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: V = lbh;  TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl);  Cube: a³, 6a²

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cylinder, cone, sphere
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Cylinder V = πr²h, CSA = 2πrh;  Cone V = ⅓πr²h;  Sphere V = 4/3 πr³, S = 4πr²

mainNarrative: For rectangles use A = lb and P = 2(l + b). A 12 m by 8 m field has area 96 m² and perimeter 40 m. For a triangle, A = ½ × base × height, and for a trapezium A = ½(a + b)h with a and b the parallel sides.
For a circle, circumference = 2πr and area = πr². With π = 22/7 and r = 7, the circumference is 44 and the area is 154. Given a circumference of 44 you can find r = 7 and then the area.
For a path around a rectangle, subtract the inner area from the outer area. A 40 m by 30 m park with a 2 m path inside: inner 36 × 26 = 936, outer 1200, path area 264 m².

For solids: cuboid V = lbh, TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl); cube V = a³, TSA = 6a²; cylinder V = πr²h, CSA = 2πrh; cone V = ⅓πr²h; sphere V = ⁴⁄₃πr³. A cylinder with r = 7 and h = 10 has V = (22/7) × 49 × 10 = 1540.
When a dimension changes by a percentage, areas change by the product of multipliers. A radius up 10% raises the area by 1.1² = 1.21, a 21% increase. Volumes change by the cube of a scale factor.

deepDiveAspects.title: Scaling
deepDiveAspects.content: If lengths are multiplied by k, areas are multiplied by k² and volumes by k³.

deepDiveAspects.title: Unit trap
deepDiveAspects.content: 1 m³ = 1000 litres, but 1 m² = 10,000 cm². Always check which unit the question wants.

solvedExamples.title: Path around a park
solvedExamples.question: A rectangular park is 40 m long and 30 m wide. A path 2 m wide runs inside along its boundary. Find the area of the path.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The path takes 2 m from each side, so the inner rectangle loses 4 m in each dimension.

solvedExamples.title: Cylinder volume
solvedExamples.question: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Base area 154 cm² times height 10 cm.

solvedExamples.title: Percentage change in radius
solvedExamples.question: The radius of a circle is increased by 10%. By what percentage does its area increase?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Area scales with the square of the radius.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Recompute the whole figure after each change.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Use k for lengths, k² for areas and k³ for volumes; for circles with r = 7k use π = 22/7.

commonMistakes.mistake: Missing the second side of a path
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: A path takes the width twice.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Check units and magnitude; options with wrong units can be removed.
